clue.text: Capable Conservative means to apply pressure

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
a bar used to exert force on something

explanation.surface: A competent Tory politician knows how to lean on people.
explanation.definitionFit: A capable person is able and quick-witted, which is a common sense of the adjective clever.

clue.text: Dead right, but not right now?

blocks.note: the late So-and-so is someone who has died
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are spot on, though perhaps not at this moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead right' reads as one phrase meaning exactly correct; split it, and the second 'right' turns out to be part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something postponed to a subsequent time happens later, not at the present moment; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

clue.text: See 16
Was plain-clothes police supremo bad?

blocks.note: to be the boss of the CID, Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, whose detectives wear plain clothes

explanation.surface: A question about whether a former head of detectives was corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: RAN means was in charge of; the CID is the detective branch of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off, especially butter or oil, is described as rancid, so the word is a synonym for bad in that sense.

clue.text: Observe law coming into force

indicators.note: something coming into another thing ends up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: an Act of Parliament is a law
to prise something open is to force it

explanation.surface: A new statute comes into effect and must be obeyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming into force' is a set phrase for a law taking effect, which hides that 'force' is a separate piece. PRACTISE is the British spelling of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a religion or custom is to observe it, carrying out its rules regularly.

clue.text: Green in place for playing birdie?

indicators.note: playing about with something moves it around, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer asks whether being on the green is the setup for a birdie putt.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture makes 'birdie' a score one under par; here it is a playful word for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine falcon is a fast bird of prey, so it is a bird, jokingly called a birdie.

clue.text: Reject ruling?

blocks.note: surface reading: to throw out a judge's or referee's decision
setter's reading: to turn down the job of ruling, as a monarch giving up the throne

explanation.walkthrough: A 'ruling' looks like a noun, an official decision; read as the act of reigning, rejecting it means renouncing the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is for a sovereign to give up the crown, refusing to go on reigning.

clue.text: Mr Woods in row about golf?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
Golf is the NATO alphabet word for G

explanation.surface: The golfer Tiger Woods is caught up in a dispute about the sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Woods is the famous golfer, so his first name identifies the man surnamed Woods.

clue.text: For hero in 21 see if grid should change

indicators.note: a request for something to change asks for it to be altered, so the letters move about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A compiler checks whether the crossword grid needs reworking to fit a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is WAGNER; the surface sounds like the setter talking about this very puzzle's grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried is the heroic protagonist of Wagner's Ring cycle, title character of its third opera.

clue.text: Nadal's grit forged where brutal conflict played out

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so the letters are remade in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rafael Nadal's determination was built on a tennis court where fierce matches were fought.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis picture makes 'played out' sound like a match; it describes a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalingrad was the city on the Volga where one of the bloodiest battles of the Second World War was fought.

clue.text: Is it Campbell in depressed Scottish area?

blocks.note: first meaning: ... Campbell, the American country singer
second meaning: a narrow valley in Scotland, low-lying ground

explanation.surface: A question about whether a Campbell is living in a deprived part of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' suggests poverty, but here it means sunk low, as a valley is. Campbell is also a Scottish clan name, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a Scottish valley, a hollow in the land, and Glen is also the first name of the singer Campbell.

clue.text: Tory lord, grand, protesting angrily do we hear?

indicators.note: asking whether we hear something points to its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
to rail against something is to protest angrily

explanation.surface: A wealthy Conservative peer is heard ranting in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Grayling, a former Conservative cabinet minister, became a life peer in 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Grayling is a Conservative member of the House of Lords, so the surname names this Tory peer.

clue.text: Artist in small restaurant for flask of wine …

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a cafe is a small informal eating place

explanation.surface: A painter sits in a bistro and orders a jug of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is an open-topped glass container in which wine is served at table.

clue.text: … like it knocked back?

definitions.note: continues the previous clue: the wine in the carafe is drunk

indicators.note: something knocked back is pushed in the opposite direction, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: as means like, in comparisons
taken as written

explanation.surface: Read with the previous clue: a flask of wine that one would happily down.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the wine over from 12 across; 'knocked back' means drunk quickly as well as reversed, so the whole phrase hints at a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, the sort of drink that gets knocked back.

clue.text: Rescue from Tank One found in drawing room

indicators.note: something found in a place is located inside it, so these pieces sit within another

blocks.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids
the Roman numeral for one
a salon is a reception room or drawing room

explanation.surface: Something is saved from a tank that turned up in a sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvation is deliverance or being saved from harm, which is what a rescue provides.

clue.text: Mingle in Session Nine?

blocks.note: taken as written
a term is a session of a school or court
the Roman numeral for nine

explanation.surface: Pupils socialise during a ninth school period or session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to the definition but is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermix is to mingle or blend things together, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Poor folk in adversity here denied name in 21 song

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the letters are put in a different order
denied means refused or withheld, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: People suffering hardship hear the name of a Wagner piece and are left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the N from the fodder before rearranging. 21 is WAGNER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ride of the Valkyries is the famous orchestral passage from Wagner's opera Die Walkure, here loosely called a song.

clue.text: Fiat lacking finish? Mine's falling apart!

indicators.note: lacking its finish means without its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a fiat is an authoritative order, a decree
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: An unfinished Fiat car prompts its owner to complain theirs is a wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiat with a capital looks like the Italian car maker, but it is an official order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decrepit is worn out and dilapidated through age or neglect, that is, falling apart.

clue.text: Good girl with detective a real looker? Hardly

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a lass is a girl
a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: A nice young woman with a detective boyfriend is not much of a beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A real looker' means an attractive person; taken literally it is an eye that genuinely sees, which an artificial one hardly is.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass eye is an artificial eye that cannot see, so it is hardly something that really looks.

clue.text: Two parties: one absolutely dead?

blocks.note: a do is a party, so two parties are that short word written twice

explanation.surface: After two parties in a row, someone feels utterly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'dead as a dodo' means completely dead, gone for good.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is the extinct flightless bird proverbial for being dead beyond any revival.

clue.text: Debt is restructured for small home

indicators.note: restructured means rebuilt in a new form, so the letters take a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A loan is renegotiated so someone can afford a tiny flat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British term for a single rented room used for both living and sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a one-room dwelling combining bedroom and sitting room, so a small home.

clue.text: Put pole in punt for renowned cycle-maker

indicators.note: to put one thing in another is to place it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: N stands for the north pole
a punt is a bet, a wager

explanation.surface: Someone pushes a pole into a punt boat in honour of a famous bicycle manufacturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' suggests a flat boat moved with a pole, but it is a bet; the 'cycle' is the Ring, not a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner composed The Ring of the Nibelung, a famous cycle of four operas.

clue.text: Family member from east entering French city

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for east
Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A relative arrives in a French city from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, one of a person's relatives.

clue.text: Mike leaving fraternity residence for pub?

indicators.note: something leaving departs from a place, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M
a fraternity is a brotherhood, so its residence is a house for men

explanation.surface: A student called Mike moves out of his frat house to live at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Fraternity suggests an American college frat house; here it simply points to men, giving MALE HOUSE before the M goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is an old word for a pub, a place selling beer.

clue.text: Ambassador seen in group in paper

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: HE is His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A diplomat is spotted among a crowd pictured in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambassadors are addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet is a single piece of paper, so the word stands for paper.

clue.text: Life-changing information stored here?

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Information that could transform someone's life is kept here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life-changing' reads as one word meaning momentous; split at the hyphen it is the fodder plus its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is a folder or computer record in which information is kept.

clue.text: The early leader whatever the compiler says?

blocks.note: pace, from Latin, means with due respect to, used when disagreeing with someone, so whatever they say
the setter is the crossword compiler, and the phrase 'pace the setter' means despite what the setter says

explanation.surface: A puzzle compiler makes a claim about who led at the start, and is brushed aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pace the setter' means with respect to the setter, that is, whatever the setter says; the pieces run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter is the runner who leads early in a race to set the speed for others.

clue.text: Start for Bukayo, inside left, yet to lose

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
inside places something within another thing, so that piece goes in the middle

blocks.note: the first letter of the footballer's name
food left on the plate is uneaten

explanation.surface: Arsenal winger Bukayo Saka starts at inside left for a team still undefeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside left' is an old football position, but here 'inside' places the letter and 'left' means not eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that has yet to lose a match is unbeaten, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Number of Premier League teams score?

blocks.note: first meaning: the count of clubs in England's top football division
second meaning: a score is an old word for that many

explanation.walkthrough: The football setting makes 'score' look like a match result; it is the old counting word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Premier League has twenty clubs, and a score is a group of twenty.
